key_insight: Algorithmic subgroup discovery revealed hidden accuracy disparities in a cardiomegaly classifier that traditional metadata-based analyses did not fully capture.
clinical_relevance: Finding underperforming patient groups could strengthen clinical AI validation and monitoring for equity and safety.
method: Identify coherent subgroups from learned feature representations.
Compare subgroup performance gaps with metadata-based analyses and assess interpretability.
Test learned subgroup annotations for bias mitigation as a proof of concept.
evidence_signal: In 223,228 chest X-rays, discovered subgroups had accuracies of 0.61–0.90 versus 0.80–0.94 for metadata-defined groups and were frequently interpretable using patient, acquisition, and model metadata.
watch_item: Evidence comes from one imaging task; generalizability and prospective monitoring benefits require further validation.
paper_title: Detection and Validation of Hidden Subgroup Disparities in Clinical AI
